CHEZ MONA / CANVAS 101 / ABOUT 5 MINUTES

Agent interactions shouldn't be limited to chat.

A canvas is an interactive workspace alongside your conversation. Use its controls yourself, ask the agent to make changes, and inspect the same result.

This canvas is an order ticket. Others can be documents, project boards, or dashboards tailored to your workflow. No coding required for this exercise.

Build an order together

Chat: the conversation where you send prompts to the agent. Canvas: this panel, where you see and change the ticket.

1. You change2. Agent changes3. You steer4. Why it matters

1 / YOU CHANGE / 45 SECONDS

A workspace, not a picture

You can work directly with the artifact instead of describing every change in chat.

Try it: click Add Omelette in the menu.

Notice: the ticket changes immediately. You made a real edit without a prompt.

2 / THE AGENT CHANGES / 75 SECONDS

Two ways to work on one ticket

The agent can use this canvas's actions to update the same order you just edited.

Try it: copy this prompt, paste it into the chat, and send it.

Add two Soups to my ticket.

Notice: watch for two Soups on your ticket. Copying a prompt does not send it or change the ticket.

3 / YOU STEER AND VERIFY / 90 SECONDS

Make a correction, then check it

You stay in control. Switch between direct edits and conversation as the work evolves.

Try it: click Remove beside Soup once on your ticket. Then send this prompt in chat.

What's on my ticket now?

Notice: compare the agent's answer with your actual ticket. Does it include your correction? You don't need to retype your edit: the agent can read the current ticket when asked.

The agent isn't automatically watching every click. It reads and changes the ticket using the capabilities provided by this canvas.

4 / WHY IT MATTERS / 90 SECONDS

The ticket is just the example

Chat helps you express intent. A canvas makes the work visible so you can inspect, steer, and verify it.

  • Release checklist: check off an item yourself, then ask the agent to add missing checks.
  • Project board: move a card, then ask the agent to reprioritize the remaining work.
  • Document: edit a paragraph, then ask the agent to revise around your changes.

A canvas can have buttons, forms, editors, or charts suited to the task. Its human controls and agent actions must be built for that workflow; not every canvas has the same capabilities.

How could I create my own?

In a new session, use /create-canvas and describe what you and the agent should each be able to do. For example: Create a release checklist canvas where I can check off items and the agent can read, add, and update them.

Take a moment: what task in your work would be easier to inspect and steer visually?
